newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for March 21.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for March 21.

text.p: One Gulf of Mexico port was reported shut Friday as a cold front in the region moved toward the Yucatan peninsula, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily meteorological report.
Crude ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state reopened early Friday after closing late Wednesday because of high wind speeds..
Other gulf ports reopened as wind velocities relaxed, with just Ciudad del Carmen reported closed. Nearby Cayo Arcas remained open to crude exports.
Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state; Salina Cruz in Oaxaca state; and Puerto Madero in Chiapas state were shut to smaller tourist and fishing ships.

The SCT warned against sailing in the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of rain and strong winds and waves. Smaller ships were warnied against sailing in the southern Gulf of Mexico and along the Yucatan peninsula and Quintana Roo coasts because of strong winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Some clouds and rains along Baja California peninsula and Sinaloa state coast. Mostly clear skies with winds 10 and 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 19 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high.
In the Gulf of Tehuantepec, winds were clocked at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/19 to 22 miles per hour) with waves seven to nine feet high expected to diminish through the day.
Cold front in eastern gulf region moving toward Yucatan peninsula with wind gusts up to 38 km/22 miles and waves six to nine feet high. Rest of coastline with winds clocked at 10 to 15 knots.
Cloudy with some rains, moderate northeastern winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
